newsitem.title: UKRAINE: AGROKHLEB-Ukraine beet crop seen up to 24-26 mln T.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Ukraine beet crop seen up to 24-26 mln T.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union, in association with Ukragroconsult, a private Ukrainian agricultural consultancy based in Kiev.
UKRAINIAN 1997 SUGARBEET OUTPUT SEEN UP TO 24-26 MLN T

KIEV, June 25 - SovEcon and Ukragroconsult's forecast for Ukrainian sugarbeet production is provisionally 24-26 million tonnes, compared to 23.0 million tonnes in 1996 and the 1991-1995 yearly average of 31.3 million tonnes.
Despite optimistic official production targets and government promises of support, the Ukrainian sugarbeet sector is likely to continue to experience problems.

This season, the state planned to increase applications of organic fertilizers by 0.7 tonnes per hectare and mineral fertilizers by 13.5 kg per hectare, to achieve average yields of 22.3 tonnes per hectare.
A greater planted area was supposed to increase sugarbeet output by 25.2 percent to 28.8 million tonnes.
None of these targets will be reached, despite Ukrainian producers' desire to continue strong refined sugar deliveries to big markets like Russia.
Officials from the National Association of Sugar Producers (the former UkrTsukor concern) rate this year's sowing campaign as unsatisfactory.
Only 20 percent of sugarbeet plantings are in good conditions, while about one third are in poor condition.
The poor results are due to late sowing, a lack of machinery and fertilizers and general mismanagement of the farm sector.
